scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: Hello, I'm on PC0 (20.1.1.x). I can't get through to
PC12 (120.1.1.x) on the far side of the network any more -- it times out
every time. I vaguely remember hearing our two sides run on "different
routing" somehow, but I honestly don't know what that means. Could someone
take a look at whatever connects the two sides and fix it? Thanks a lot!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — PC0 (20.1.1.10) unable to reach PC12 (120.1.1.10) — does
not reflect the actual state of the network. Comprehensive testing shows
full bidirectional connectivity with 0% packet loss and confirmed end-to-end
traceroute: PC0 → r1 (20.1.1.1) → r11 (111.1.1.2) → r12 (112.1.1.2) → PC12.

The two "different routing" domains the user vaguely recalled are OSPF (area 3,
covering r1 and the broader left-side infrastructure) and EIGRP AS 100 (covering
the right-side stub routers r11, r12, and r13). Router r11 is the deliberate
redistribution boundary: it participates in both protocols, announcing its EIGRP
topology into OSPF via "redistribute eigrp" so that the OSPF side can reach the
120.0.0.0/8 segment attached to r12. The OSPF adjacency between r1 and r11
(eth1/111.0.0.0/8, area 3) is in Full/DR state with timers healthy. The EIGRP
adjacency between r11 and r12 (eth0/112.0.0.0/8) is established and stable.
Route 120.0.0.0/8 is present in r1 as an OSPF external (distance 110, metric 20,
via 111.1.1.2), in r11 as an EIGRP route (distance 90, metric 30720, via
112.1.1.2), and directly connected on r12. The reverse path is equally sound: r11
carries 20.0.0.0/8 as an OSPF route via r1, and r12 uses a kernel default route
(0.0.0.0/0 via r11) to reach the OSPF domain.

Root cause: there is no fault; the user's report is a false premise. No corrective
action is required.
